reviewer: Codex independent scientific reviewer B, not original text/profile author
scope: Seven actual changed scientific descriptions; other current decisions are inherited unchanged

rows.atomicityReason: Carboxyl-group recognition, acidic-character observation and homologous structural representation are linked evidence for recognizing this substance class. The clarified observation is not falsely exclusive analytical identification. Separate nomenclature and intermolecular-property source companions remain distinct.
rows.memoryReason: The learner interprets unfamiliar structures and observations and writes corresponding formulas; structures and comparison data may be supplied. A separate compact recall module is not needed to prove this recognition/representation competence. No existing memory goal or card is removed.

rows.atomicityReason: One reaction-interpretation competence distinguishes acidic ester equilibria from net alkaline carboxylate formation. Product balance and everyday explanation test that same condition-sensitive model; the separate LK mechanism remains separate.
rows.memoryReason: Given ester structures and reaction conditions support an unfamiliar product/charge balance and causal comparison. Memorizing a substrate list is insufficient and a separate recall deck is unnecessary for this competence.

rows.atomicityReason: A single practical preparation chain includes actual alkaline fat hydrolysis, product explanation and salting-out separation of the soap. Glycerol and fatty-acid salts are correct, and salting out does not itself cleave the fat. Actual practical execution remains assessable and cannot be inferred from an image or supplied log.
rows.memoryReason: Authorized supervised protocols, substrate formulas and controls may be supplied; mastery is practical execution plus explanation/observation. A separate fact-recall module would not certify that performance and is not required by the clarified competence.

rows.atomicityReason: One amphiphilic structure-to-arrangement model explains interfaces, micelles, emulsification and surface-tension reduction. An oil droplet is distinguished from a micelle; unrelated quantitative soap-pH measurement is not absorbed into this goal.
rows.memoryReason: The learner transfers a supplied amphiphile structure to a fresh interface and explains the arrangement and property. A diagram label recalled without causal transfer cannot pass; a compact independent recall module is unnecessary.

rows.atomicityReason: One washing-system model relates controlled changes of temperature, water hardness and concentration to dispersal, micelles and insoluble hardness soaps. The factors are conditions of the same competence; no universal optimum, arbitrary titration or unrelated experimental routine is added.
rows.memoryReason: Data tables, structures and ionic charges can be supplied. The required performance is causal explanation and comparison under controlled conditions; a separate memorized temperature/dose table would not establish the goal.

rows.atomicityReason: A single water-hardness model distinguishes temporary, permanent and total hardness and explains suitable removal mechanisms. The title no longer promises an unrequired complexometric quantification; total hardness is restored. The specified calcium heating model does not imply universal MgCO3 formation, and ion exchange is not desalination.
rows.memoryReason: Ion composition and the specified exchanger/precipitation model may be supplied; unfamiliar hardness attribution and charge balance are assessed. A separate salt-list recall module is not required for this explanation competence.

rows.atomicityReason: One practical qualitative evidence chain performs the test with authorized protocol/controls and explains reagent reduction by ascorbate. Ascorbate is the antioxidant, not the act of testing. Generic reducing response is not falsely exclusive identification in an arbitrary mixture.
rows.memoryReason: A valid supervised protocol, reagent information and redox model can be supplied. Actual execution, controlled observation and electron-transfer explanation are required; recalling a reagent/color alone would not establish mastery. No separate recall deck is needed.
